research.website_note: The results show buttondown.com as Buttondown’s own official site and docs, so the website belongs to the named company.

strategy.observation: Buttondown already markets one-click concierge migration and says it can move customers within one business day.
strategy.offer_link: Because Buttondown already has a migration motion, outside help focused on writers leaving Substack could slot into that workflow as extra capacity or more Substack-specific migration expertise.
hypotheses: Buttondown wants to acquire more writers from Substack.
Migration requests are a meaningful part of their acquisition or support workload.
They would consider outside help if it reduced manual migration effort or sped up onboarding.
strategy.angle: Buttondown already has one-click concierge migration, so I’m reaching out with Substack-specific migration help that could take some of that work off your team.
strategy.fit_reason: The fit is plausible because Buttondown clearly cares about migrations, but it is also somewhat redundant because they already offer their own fast concierge migration. External help would only matter if they want extra capacity or a narrower Substack-specific service.

draft.subject: Substack migration support
draft.body:
Noticed Buttondown already offers one-click concierge migration and says it can move customers within a business day.

I help newsletter writers move off Substack by handling the messy parts of the transfer, so your team doesn’t have to spend as much time on manual setup.

If Substack migrations are coming in steadily, could outside help fit into that workflow as overflow support?
